name: Vancomycin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Intravenous vancomycin needs kidney-based dose adjustment guided by serum concentrations. The US label sets an initial dose of no less than 15 mg/kg at any level of kidney function, then dosing by measured levels. The 2020 consensus guideline recommends weight-based loading that is not reduced for kidney function and area-under-the-curve (AUC) guided maintenance (target 400 to 600 mg·h/L).
kidney_function_basis: Label gives no fixed eGFR or CrCl bands; dosing is concentration-guided.

bands.recommendation: 15–20 mg/kg (actual body weight) every 8–12 hours; AUC-guided (target 400–600 mg·h/L) (Rybak 2020). Label alternative: 2 g/day (0.5 g every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours), adjusted to serum concentrations.

Loading dose is not reduced for kidney function: 20–35 mg/kg actual body weight (maximum 3 g) if critically ill (Rybak 2020). Then extend the interval and adjust maintenance by AUC or serum concentrations (label: initial dose no less than 15 mg/kg).

Loading dose is not reduced for kidney function: 20–35 mg/kg actual body weight (maximum 3 g) if critically ill (Rybak 2020). Maintenance by AUC or serum concentrations (label: initial dose no less than 15 mg/kg).

Loading dose is not reduced for kidney function: 20–35 mg/kg actual body weight (maximum 3 g) if critically ill (Rybak 2020). Functionally anephric (label): measure a level at 24 hours to guide further dosing.

hd.text: Loading dose by actual body weight (do not reduce for kidney function). Maintenance after each HD session (or during the last 60–90 minutes), adjusted to pre-dialysis concentrations: a pre-HD level of 15–20 mg/L is likely to achieve AUC 400–600 mg·h/L; check at least weekly (Rybak 2020).
hd.short: Load; redose each HD; pre-HD level 15–20

pd.text: PD peritonitis: intraperitoneal vancomycin per the ISPD 2022 guideline (weight-based intermittent dosing; redose guided by serum levels); see the guideline for doses. Vancomycin enters peritoneal dialysis fluid (label). Specialist input.

crrt.text: At effluent 20–25 mL/kg/h: loading 20–25 mg/kg actual body weight, then 7.5–10 mg/kg every 12 hours; check levels within 24 hours; continuous infusion is an alternative (Rybak 2020). Hybrid/SLED: load 20–25 mg/kg, then 15 mg/kg after or during the last 60–90 minutes.

dialyzable: Yes with high-flux HD (substantial removal each session; the label's 'poorly removed' statement reflects older low-flux membranes). Give maintenance doses after HD or during the last part of the session.
monitoring: Serum concentrations (AUC-guided, target 400–600 mg·h/L, per consensus; trough per label); pre-dialysis levels at least weekly on hemodialysis; serum creatinine; nephrotoxicity risk rises with other nephrotoxins.

pediatric.approved_ages: Indicated in pediatric patients (label). This premixed product is not recommended when the needed dose is not 500 mg, 750 mg, 1 g, 1.25 g or 1.5 g; use another formulation.
pediatric.usual_dose: ≥3 months, serious MRSA: 60–80 mg/kg/day divided every 6–8 hours, AUC-guided (Rybak 2020); usual maximum 3,600 mg/day. Label: 10 mg/kg every 6 hours.

renal.recommendation: ≥3 months, serious MRSA: 60–80 mg/kg/day divided every 6–8 hours, AUC-guided (Rybak 2020). Label: 10 mg/kg every 6 hours.
Initial dose no less than 15 mg/kg; maintenance by serum concentrations (label applies to 'patients with any degree of renal impairment').
Initial dose no less than 15 mg/kg; maintenance by serum concentrations.
15 mg/kg initial dose; level at 24 hours to guide dosing.

hd.text: Level-guided dosing; specialist (pediatric nephrology/infectious diseases) input.

pediatric.neonates: Neonates (label): initial 15 mg/kg, then 10 mg/kg every 12 hours in the first week of life and every 8 hours thereafter up to 1 month of age.
pediatric.notes: Neonates and infants up to 3 months: 10–20 mg/kg every 8–48 hours by postmenstrual age, weight and serum creatinine (Rybak 2020).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
